flagged.evidence: The item says cobounded means some bounded subset B has G·B=X, and then claims equivalently there are x_0 in X and R>=0 with every point within R of G·x_0. But [def-metric-bounded-diameter] explicitly defines a bounded subset by “A is bounded if A = emptyset or ...”. Therefore on the empty metric space X=emptyset any action is cobounded by the first clause, taking B=emptyset so G·B=emptyset=X, while the claimed equivalent clause is impossible because there is no x_0 in X. The equivalence needs a nonempty-space hypothesis.

As written, X may be empty. By [def-geodesic-and-geodesic-metric-space], an empty metric space is geodesic vacuously, and by the current [def-isometric-proper-and-cobounded-actions-on-metric-spaces] any group acts geometrically on X=emptyset. Then taking G=Z and H=F_2, this Statement asserts they are quasi-isometric. But [ex-growth-of-free-abelian-groups] gives polynomial growth for Z, [thm-free-groups-of-rank-at-least-two-have-exponential-growth] gives exponential growth for F_2, and [thm-growth-type-is-a-quasi-isometry-invariant-of-finitely-generated-groups] rules out a quasi-isometry. So the Statement needs a nonempty-space hypothesis (or an explicit basepoint/orbit-map formulation).

The composite-degree claim says “for every proper divisor d of n the congruence classes modulo d form a nontrivial block system.” Take n=4 and d=1. Then the congruence classes modulo 1 give the one-block partition of Z/4Z, which is trivial, not nontrivial. The proof itself uses “Because 1<d<n” in step 2.1, but step 1.2 assumes only “d be a proper divisor”. The claim needs d to be a nontrivial proper divisor.
